atoms.b: Techno-utopianism is the belief that ((scientific --horrific)) and technological progress can create a better future by ((improving --controlling)) people's lives and solving existential challenges such as disease, poverty and ((climate --government)) change.

A key area of research linked to techno-utopianism is ((human --digital)) enhancement, which uses technology to improve humans' physical and mental abilities beyond their natural limits. Technologies such as ((artificial --official)) intelligence, gene editing, brain implants, and ((robotics --ethics)) could make people healthier, smarter and live longer.

However, not everyone agrees with this ((optimistic --pessimistic)) view. Critics argue that these technologies could also create new risks, increase ((inequality --equality)) or raise difficult ethical questions.

flip.text:
Brain implants
Researchers are developing brain–computer interfaces that could allow people with paralysis to control robotic limbs or wheelchairs using their thoughts. These implants could also be used to increase intelligence or to help people with memory loss.

Gene editing
Scientists are researching the possibility of making precise changes to DNA, which would allow them to treat inherited diseases. The same technology could be used to reduce the risk of certain genetic diseases before a child is born.

Anti-ageing medicine
Researchers are studying drugs designed to remove damaged cells which contribute to ageing and age-related diseases. Eventually, these treatments could expand the human life span.

atoms.b: Some risks apply to ((several --digital)) technologies. For example, life-((extending --changing)) treatments could be so expensive that they remain available only to the wealthy. Similarly, brain ((implants --injuries)) designed to enhance intelligence could ((increase --decrease)) inequality by giving certain groups an artificial advantage. Unequal ((access --advantage)) to gene editing could also lead to discrimination against people whose parents could not ((afford --bother)) to enhance their appearance or abilities.
